title: Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection
summary: Existing text anomaly detection methods only work at the document level (or on narrow, task-specific token tasks such as spell checking), so they cannot localize which tokens in a text are anomalous. The paper introduces token-level text anomaly detection, releases three token-annotated benchmarks (SMS_Spam with injected character corruption, Restaurant Review semantic anomalies, Grammar errors), and proposes TokenCore, which builds a memory bank of normal word-level token embeddings (BERT-base-uncased embeddings aggregated by element-wise max pooling over subwords) and scores each test token by its nearest-neighbor distance, aggregating token scores by mean for document-level scores. TokenCore achieves the best average token-level AUROC (0.7145) and document-level AUROC (0.7335) among 7 methods, ranking first at token level on Review (0.8271) and Grammar (0.6371) and at document level on Review (0.9594), while ECOD/iForest remain better on the character-corruption SMS_Spam token-level task.

target.split: Test = 50% of documents not used as normal training data (normal + anomalous); token-level scoring over test documents

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

why: The authors released the method code (TokenCore.py: memory bank + nearest-neighbor token scoring), the alignment/annotation utilities (align.py, tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py) and all three annotated datasets locally in data/ (grammar .npy/.json, restaurant_review, sms_spam), so the core logic can be kept verbatim. What is NOT released is a runnable entrypoint: the only end-to-end artifact is Demo.ipynb (with frozen outputs), there is no requirements.txt, and TokenCore.py consumes precomputed token-embedding matrices, so the BERT-base-uncased embedding extraction, the 50/50 split and the token-level AUROC computation have to be rebuilt as a script from the notebook before the target number for Grammar (C1) can be produced. Keep authors' logic, rebuild the missing driver.
est_runtime: ~25-35 min wall clock on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM: ~10 min installing torch (CPU wheel), transformers, scikit-learn; ~1 min BERT-base download; ~1-3 min BERT forward pass over 300 short Grammar documents; seconds for the max-pooling, memory-bank build and brute-force nearest-neighbor scoring; plus the driver-script rewrite from the notebook and one clean end-to-end re-run.
blockers: no dependency file: torch/transformers/sklearn/numpy must be pinned by hand (works on Python 3.12)
TokenCore.py takes embedding matrices only; the BERT max-pooling-over-subwords front-end exists only inside the notebook, so the pipeline must be extracted into a script
Demo.ipynb is 3.8 MB of stored outputs; it must be rewritten/cleared before execution
no GPU on this machine (BERT-base CPU inference only, which is acceptable at this scale)

Grammar token-level AUROC is computed over very few anomalous tokens (~15 anomalous docs in the test half), and the split is random, so the absolute value 0.6371 will depend on the split seed and may drift

approach: This is a partial_release reproduction of claim C1: TokenCore's token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (0.6371, tolerance ±0.02 absolute). We clone the authors' repo, keep TokenCore.py/align.py/json_to_npy.py verbatim, and rebuild only the missing driver that Demo.ipynb used to hide: read the released grammar annotations (data/grammar_correction_labeled.json and data/grammar.npy), build the 300-document corpus (270 normal / 30 anomalous, R10), take 50% of the normal documents as the memory-bank training set (R6, A8), run BERT-base-uncased over the remaining normal + anomalous documents, max-pool subword embeddings into word units aligned with the gold word-level token labels (Eq. 1, R2/R9, A3/A4), fit the authors' TextCore memory bank on normal-training token embeddings only (R3, A2), score every test token by Euclidean nearest-neighbour distance (Eq. 2, R4, A1/A9), and compute pooled token-level AUROC/AUPRC plus the mean-aggregated document-level scores (Eq. 3, R5, A5). The paper value is a single split-free number, so the only real drift risk is split randomness on 300 short documents; we therefore report a primary seeded run plus a small multi-seed spread so the ±0.02 band can be interpreted. Only the Grammar dataset is needed for C1, but the same driver is written so that running it on restaurant_review / sms_spam later costs nothing extra.
steps: Clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git into ./TokenCore and record the commit hash; do not modify TokenCore.py, align.py or tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py.

Create a venv/conda env on Python 3.12 and pip install torch (CPU wheel from the default index), transformers, numpy, scikit-learn, tqdm, requests; write the resolved versions into requirements.txt (the file the README references but the repo lacks).

Run src/inspect_data.py: dump shapes/dtypes/keys of data/grammar.npy and the JSON schema of data/grammar_correction_labeled.json, and print the actual class/function signatures of TokenCore.py and align.py. Decide the exact field names for words, token labels and document labels, and confirm the .npy is a token/label array rather than precomputed embeddings (43 KB is far too small for 300x768 floats).

Implement src/data_grammar.py against the inspected schema; load all 300 Grammar documents and hard-assert 300 documents / 270 normal / 30 anomalous (10% rate, R10) and consistency of the document labels with the token labels (R11).

Implement the split: with seed 0, shuffle the 270 normal documents, take the first 135 as the memory-bank training set; the test set is the other 135 normal documents plus all 30 anomalous documents (165 docs). Export the token-level gold labels for every test token.

Implement src/embed_bert.py: tokenize with BertTokenizerFast(return_offsets_mapping / word_ids), run BertModel in eval() with torch.no_grad() in batches of 32, max_length 128, take last_hidden_state, drop special tokens, and element-wise max-pool subwords per word unit. Assert a 1:1 map between produced word units and the gold word tokens in the annotated JSON; if align.py exposes an alignment helper, call it instead of re-implementing.

Implement src/detector.py: import the authors' TokenCore (use the real class name found by inspect_data.py, README shows both TokenCore and TextCore) and its fit / decision_function, fit on the normal-training token embedding matrix (no anomalous tokens, R3) and score the test token embeddings (R4).

Implement src/evaluate.py: token-level AUROC/AUPRC pooled over all test tokens (micro), document-level scores as the per-document mean of token scores (R5) and their AUROC/AUPRC, plus a random-score control (expected AUROC ~0.5) to validate the metric plumbing.
Wire reproduce.py to run the whole chain end-to-end; run the smoke configuration first (see smoke_test) and confirm all assertions on counts and shapes pass.
Run the intermediate checks (see intermediate_checks) before the full run.

Full run: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --seed 0 (CPU-only BERT inference over 300 short sentences, seconds for the memory bank and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour search). Write results/metrics.json.

If |token_auroc_grammar - 0.6371| > 0.02, re-run with seeds 1 and 2 and inspect sensitivity: report the per-seed values and mean/std, and check the highest-risk choices first (A5 micro vs per-document AUROC, A1/A9 Euclidean on unnormalized embeddings, A4 whether punctuation units are scored).
Write the final results/metrics.json containing the primary value, the multi-seed spread, the target, the tolerance band and an explicit pass/fail flag.
smoke_test: python reproduce.py --datasets grammar --smoke --seed 0 -> loads the released grammar annotations, keeps only the first 8 normal + first 2 anomalous documents (forcing the split so both sides are non-empty), runs one BERT-base forward pass over those 10 documents, max-pools subwords, builds a ~100-200 entry memory bank, scores the test tokens, and prints token_auroc/token_auprc plus every shape (n_docs, n_word_units, n_bank_tokens, n_test_tokens, n_positive_tokens). Success = no exception, finite scores, 1:1 alignment between word units and gold tokens, and AUROC in [0,1]. This exercises every stage of the data flow in under a minute.
intermediate_checks: Dataset size and label rate: exactly 300 documents, 270 normal (token_labels all 0) and 30 anomalous (>=1 token_label = 1) = 10% anomaly rate (R10); stop if the released file deviates.
Document/token label consistency: every document with at least one 1 token has doc_label 1 and vice versa (R11).

Token-level class balance: report total tokens, total anomalous tokens and their fraction across all 300 docs, and across the 165 test docs; sanity expectation is a few percent (the contract quotes token AUPRC ~0.04 for Grammar, which is roughly the positive rate) and only a handful of positives, so AUROC variance across seeds will be large - this justifies the ±0.02 band.
Alignment coverage: fraction of gold word tokens that receive a BERT word unit (target 1.0); log any word that tokenizes to zero subwords or overflows max_length=128.
Split sizes: 135 normal training docs and 135 normal + 30 anomalous test docs with seed 0; training set contains zero anomalous tokens (R3).

Memory bank size: n_bank_tokens should equal the total number of word units in the 135 normal training documents (report it; expect a few thousand) - a much smaller number means documents were dropped silently.

Parameter/embedding check: assert the token embedding width is 768 and that the pooling really is element-wise max (a max-pooled vector must equal the coordinate-wise max of its subword vectors on a hand-checked example).

Sanity baseline: random token scores give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~positive rate; TokenCore scores on the training tokens themselves (excluding self-matches) give near-zero distances, confirming the nearest-neighbour direction (higher distance = more anomalous, R4).
Metric parity: verify the AUROC/AUPRC implementation against sklearn.roc_auc_score / average_precision_score on synthetic labels, so the 0.6371 comparison cannot fail for plumbing reasons.
budget_plan: Total ~30-35 min on 22 CPU cores / 15.4 GB RAM. Setup 10 min: clone the repo (<1 min) and pip install the CPU torch wheel plus transformers/scikit-learn (~8-9 min, ~5 GB, the dominant cost). Reconnaissance 3 min: inspect_data.py plus reading TokenCore.py/align.py and the JSON schema. Implementation 8 min: data_grammar.py, embed_bert.py, detector.py, evaluate.py, reproduce.py, requirements.txt. Smoke 2 min: 10-document subset end-to-end. Intermediate checks 2 min: counts, rates, alignment coverage, bank size, metric parity. Full run 3-4 min: one BERT-base forward pass over 300 short Grammar sentences on CPU (1-3 min) plus seconds of max-pooling and brute-force L2 nearest-neighbour scoring. Verification 3 min: compare against 0.6371 with the ±0.02 band, and if out of band spend up to 5 more minutes on seeds 1 and 2 and on the highest-risk assumptions (A5, A1/A9, A4). Keep ~3 min slack; only the Grammar dataset is run, so no SMS_Spam/Review time is spent.

    4| class TokenCore:
    5|     """
    6|     TokenCore anomaly detector based on nearest neighbor distances
    7|     """
    8|     def __init__(self, n_neighbors=1, aggregation='max'):
    9|         """
   10|         Parameters
   11|         ----------
   12|         n_neighbors : int, default=1
   13|             Number of neighbors to use
   14|         aggregation : str, default='mean'
   15|             How to aggregate distances when n_neighbors > 1
   16|             Options: 'mean', 'max', 'min', 'median'
   17|         """
   18|         self.n_neighbors = n_neighbors
   19|         self.aggregation = aggregation
   20|         self.nbrs = None
   21|         
   22|     def fit(self, X):
   23|         """
   24|         Fit the model using X as training data
   25|         
   26|         Parameters
   27|         ----------
   28|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   29|             Training data
   30|             
   31|         Returns
   32|         -------
   33|         self : object
   34|             Fitted estimator
   35|         """
   36|         self.nbrs = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=self.n_neighbors).fit(X)
   37|         return self
   38|     
   39|     def decision_function(self, X):
   40|         """
   41|         Compute anomaly scores for samples in X
   42|         
   43|         Parameters
   44|         ----------
   45|         X : array-like of shape (n_samples, n_features)
   46|             Test data
   47|             
   48|         Returns
   49|         -------
   50|         scores : array-like of shape (n_samples,)
   51|             Anomaly scores (higher means more anomalous)
   52|         """
   53|         distances, _ = self.nbrs.kneighbors(X)
   54|         
   55|         # If n_neighbors == 1, distances is (n_samples, 1), just flatten
   56|         if self.n_neighbors == 1:
   57|             scores = distances.flatten()
   58|         else:
   59|             # Aggregate multiple neighbor distances
   60|             if self.aggregation == 'mean':
   61|                 scores = np.mean(distances, axis=1)
   62|             elif self.aggregation == 'max':
   63|                 scores = np.max(distances, axis=1)
   64|             elif self.aggregation == 'min':
   65|                 scores = np.min(distances, axis=1)
   66|             elif self.aggregation == 'median':
   67|                 scores = np.median(distances, axis=1)
   68|             else:
   69|                 raise ValueError(f"Unknown aggregation method: {self.aggregation}")
   70|         
   71|         return scores

    1| # TokenCore
    2| 
    3| Official code and datasets for the paper
    4| **[Towards Token-Level Text Anomaly Detection](https://huggingface.co/papers/2601.13644)** (WWW '26).
    5| 
    6| TokenCore is a memory-bank method for **token-level text anomaly detection**: instead of only flagging whole documents as anomalous, it localizes *which specific tokens* are anomalous. It builds a memory bank of normal token embeddings and scores each test token by its distance to the nearest normal neighbor, then aggregates token scores to obtain document-level scores.
    7| 
    8| ## Datasets
    9| 
   10| The three benchmark datasets are hosted on the Hugging Face Hub:
   11| 
   12| 👉 **[https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Charles-Cao/TokenAD)**
   13| 
   14| Each dataset provides both document-level and token-level anomaly annotations.
   15| 
   16| | Dataset | Anomaly type | Documents | Anomalies | Rate |
   17| |---|---|---|---|---|
   18| | SMS Spam | Character-level (corrupted sequences) | 4,518 | 393 | 8.7% |
   19| | Restaurant Review | Semantic (negative sentiment) | 1,100 | 50 | 4.5% |
   20| | Grammar Correction | Grammatical errors | 300 | 30 | 10% |
   21| 
   22| A local copy is also available in the `data/` folder.
   23| 
   24| ## Installation
   25| 
   26| ```bash
   27| git clone https://github.com/charles-cao/TokenCore.git
   28| cd TokenCore
   29| pip install -r requirements.txt
   30| ```
   31| 
   32| ## Quick Start
   33| 
   34| ```python
   35| from TokenCore import TextCore
   36| 
   37| model = TokenCore()
   38| 
   39| # Fit on normal token embeddings
   40| model.fit(X_train)
   41| 
   42| # Get token-level anomaly scores
   43| scores = model.decision_function(X_test)
   44| ```
   45| 
   46| `X_train` and `X_test` are token embedding matrices (e.g. BERT embeddings with max-pooling over subwords). See `Demo.ipynb` for the full pipeline, including embedding extraction, token-level scoring, and document-level aggregation.
   47| 
   48| ## Repository Structure
   49|

   51| TokenCore/
   52| ├── data/           # Benchmark datasets (also on Hugging Face Hub)
   53| ├── TokenCore.py     # TokenCore method implementation
   54| ├── Demo.ipynb      # End-to-end demo of the key steps
   55| └── README.md
   56| ```

applications.
Anomaly Detection Methods. Traditional anomaly detection
algorithms can be broadly categorized into density-based, isolation-
based, statistical, and deep learning approaches. Density-based
methods like LOF [1] identify anomalies by measuring local density
deviations relative to neighboring points. Isolation-based meth-
ods [2] such as Isolation Forest [8] exploit the property that anom-
alies are sparse and easier to isolate through random partitioning.
Statistical approaches including ECOD [7] detect anomalies through
their deviation from estimated data distributions using cumulative
distribution functions. Deep learning methods like Deep SVDD [11]
and AutoEncoder learn compact representations of normal data
and identify anomalies as points with high reconstruction error or
large distance from the learned hypersphere. More recent methods
like LUNAR [5] combine nearest neighbor information with neural

"""Load the released Grammar Correction benchmark and build the 50%-normal training split.

Data source: repo/data/grammar.npy (the released TokenCore benchmark, produced by
repo/tokens_labels/json_to_npy.py from data/grammar_correction_labeled.json).
Keys: 'sentences' (list of [str]), 'tokens' (list of list[str]), 'labels' (list of list[int]).

Paper Sec. 4 / requirement R10: 270 correct (normal) + 30 incorrect (anomalous) = 300 documents,
10% anomaly rate.  Requirement R11: a document is anomalous iff it contains >= 1 anomalous token.
Paper Sec. 6.1 / requirement R6: 50% of the normal documents are the training (memory-bank) set,
the remaining normal + all anomalous documents form the test set.
"""
import numpy as np

DATA_PATH = "repo/data/grammar.npy"


def load_grammar(path=DATA_PATH):
    """Return a list of document dicts with gold word-level tokens and token labels."""
    raw = np.load(path, allow_pickle=True).item()
    sentences = [s[0] if isinstance(s, (list, tuple, np.ndarray)) else s for s in raw["sentences"]]
    tokens = [list(t) for t in raw["tokens"]]
    labels = [[int(x) for x in lab] for lab in raw["labels"]]

    assert len(sentences) == len(tokens) == len(labels), "ragged benchmark file"
    docs = []
    for i, (sent, tok, lab) in enumerate(zip(sentences, tokens, labels)):
        assert len(tok) == len(lab), f"doc {i}: {len(tok)} tokens vs {len(lab)} labels"
        docs.append({
            "doc_id": i,
            "sentence": sent,
            "words": tok,
            "token_labels": lab,
            "doc_label": 1 if any(lab) else 0,
        })
    return docs


def dataset_stats(docs):
    n_docs = len(docs)
    n_anom_docs = sum(d["doc_label"] for d in docs)
    n_tokens = sum(len(d["words"]) for d in docs)
    n_anom_tokens = sum(sum(d["token_labels"]) for d in docs)
    return {
        "n_docs": n_docs,
        "n_normal_docs": n_docs - n_anom_docs,
        "n_anomalous_docs": n_anom_docs,
        "doc_anomaly_rate": n_anom_docs / n_docs,
        "n_tokens": n_tokens,
        "n_anomalous_tokens": n_anom_tokens,
        "token_anomaly_rate": n_anom_tokens / n_tokens,
    }


def split_anomaly_data(docs, seed=0, train_frac=0.5):
    """Rebuild of the missing `eval.split_anomaly_data` used by Demo.ipynb.

    Returns (X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test) where
      X_* = list of gold word-token lists (one per document)
      y_* = document-level labels (1 iff >= 1 anomalous token, R11)
      z_* = token-level labels (list of list[int])
    """
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    normal = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d["doc_label"] == 0])
    anom = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d["doc_label"] == 1])

    rng.shuffle(normal)
    n_train = int(round(len(normal) * train_frac))
    train_idx = normal[:n_train]
    test_idx = np.concatenate([normal[n_train:], anom])
    rng.shuffle(test_idx)

    def gather(idx):
        X = [docs[i]["words"] for i in idx]
        y = [docs[i]["doc_label"] for i in idx]
        z = [docs[i]["token_labels"] for i in idx]
        return X, y, z

    X_train, y_train, z_train = gather(train_idx)
    X_test, y_test, z_test = gather(test_idx)
    return X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test


def check_dataset(docs):
    """Hard assertions from R10 / R11; raise if the released file deviates."""
    st = dataset_stats(docs)
    assert st["n_docs"] == 300, f"expected 300 documents, got {st['n_docs']}"
    assert st["n_anomalous_docs"] == 30, f"expected 30 anomalous documents, got {st['n_anomalous_docs']}"
    assert st["n_normal_docs"] == 270, f"expected 270 normal documents, got {st['n_normal_docs']}"
    assert abs(st["doc_anomaly_rate"] - 0.10) < 1e-9, f"expected 10% anomaly rate, got {st['doc_anomaly_rate']}"
    for d in docs:
        assert d["doc_label"] == (1 if any(d["token_labels"]) else 0), \
            f"doc {d['doc_id']}: doc_label inconsistent with token labels (R11)"
    return st


if __name__ == "__main__":
    docs = load_grammar()
    print("stats:", check_dataset(docs))
    Xtr, ytr, Xte, yte, ztr, zte = split_anomaly_data(docs, seed=0)
    print("train docs:", len(Xtr), "anomalous train docs:", sum(ytr),
          "train tokens:", sum(len(t) for t in Xtr),
          "anomalous train tokens:", sum(sum(z) for z in ztr))
    print("test docs:", len(Xte), "anomalous test docs:", sum(yte),
          "test tokens:", sum(len(t) for t in Xte),
          "anomalous test tokens:", sum(sum(z) for z in zte))

"""BERT front-end: word-level embeddings by element-wise max pooling over subwords.

The pooling / alignment logic is taken VERBATIM from the authors' repo/align.py
(`extract_word_embeddings`), which is the code Demo.ipynb used to build the token
embedding matrices fed to TokenCore.  We only add:
  * stdout suppression (align.py prints an alignment trace per sentence),
  * a 1:1 alignment assertion against the gold word tokens,
  * an on-disk cache of the resulting matrices (embeddings depend only on the
    backbone, not on the train/test split, so they are computed once per model).

Paper Sec. 5 Eq. (1) / requirements R1, R2, R9:
  e_token = max(e_1, ..., e_n)  element-wise over the subwords of the word.
Special tokens ([CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]) are skipped (word_idx is None) exactly as in align.py.
"""
import contextlib
import io
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

REPO = os.path.abspath("repo")
if REPO not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO)

from align import extract_word_embeddings  # noqa: E402  (authors' code, unmodified)


def _cache_dir():
    """Directory for reusable raw artefacts (models, embedding caches)."""
    base = os.environ.get("REPRO_DATA_CACHE")
    if not base:
        base = os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".cache", "tokencore")
    d = os.path.join(base, "tokencore_embeddings")
    os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
    return d


def embed_documents(all_tokens, all_labels, model_name, device="cpu", verbose=False):
    """Run the authors' align.extract_word_embeddings over a list of documents.

    Returns a list (one entry per document) of lists of dicts
    {'token', 'embedding' (np.ndarray[768]), 'label'}.
    """
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = model.to(device).eval()

    sink = io.StringIO()
    ctx = contextlib.redirect_stdout(sink) if not verbose else contextlib.nullcontext()
    with ctx, __import__("torch").no_grad():
        out = extract_word_embeddings(
            model=model,
            tokenizer=tokenizer,
            all_tokens=all_tokens,
            all_labels=all_labels,
            model_name=model_name,
            local_cache_dir=None,
            device=device,
        )
    if not verbose:
        sys.stderr.write(sink.getvalue()[-2000:] if os.environ.get("TOKENCORE_DEBUG") else "")
    return out


def embed_all(docs, model_name, device="cpu", use_cache=True, verbose=False):
    """Embed every document once; cache to REPRO_DATA_CACHE. Returns per-doc dicts."""
    tag = model_name.replace("/", "__")
    cache = os.path.join(_cache_dir(), f"grammar_{tag}.npz")
    if use_cache and os.path.exists(cache):
        blob = np.load(cache, allow_pickle=True)
        return [list(s) for s in blob["docs"]]

    out = embed_documents([d["words"] for d in docs], [d["token_labels"] for d in docs],
                          model_name, device=device, verbose=verbose)

    # --- alignment / sanity checks (R2, R9) -----------------------------------
    n_units = 0
    for d, sent in zip(docs, out):
        assert len(sent) == len(d["words"]), (
            f"doc {d['doc_id']}: {len(sent)} word units vs {len(d['words'])} gold tokens")
        for item, gold_word, gold_lab in zip(sent, d["words"], d["token_labels"]):
            assert item["token"] == gold_word, (
                f"doc {d['doc_id']}: unit '{item['token']}' != gold '{gold_word}'")
            assert int(item["label"]) == int(gold_lab), (
                f"doc {d['doc_id']}: label mismatch for '{gold_word}'")
            emb = np.asarray(item["embedding"], dtype=np.float32)
            assert emb.shape == (768,), f"unexpected embedding shape {emb.shape}"
            item["embedding"] = emb
            n_units += 1

    if use_cache:
        np.savez(cache, docs=np.array(out, dtype=object), model=np.array(model_name))
    return out


def flatten(docs_embeddings):
    """(X, z, doc_index) with X = (n_tokens, 768) matrix, z = token labels."""
    X, z, doc_of = [], [], []
    for i, sent in enumerate(docs_embeddings):
        for item in sent:
            X.append(np.asarray(item["embedding"], dtype=np.float32))
            z.append(int(item["label"]))
            doc_of.append(i)
    return np.asarray(X, dtype=np.float32), np.asarray(z, dtype=int), np.asarray(doc_of, dtype=int)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    import data_grammar
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    print(data_grammar.check_dataset(docs))
    emb = embed_all(docs[:10], "bert-base-cased", use_cache=False, verbose=False)
    X, z, doc_of = flatten(emb)
    print("X", X.shape, "z", z.shape, "positives", int(z.sum()), "docs", len(emb))

"""Thin adapter over the authors' UNMODIFIED repo/TokenCore.py.

The released class is `TokenCore` (memory bank + sklearn NearestNeighbors,
n_neighbors=1 -> score = distance to the single nearest normal neighbour, i.e.
paper Eq. (2)).  NearestNeighbors' default metric is Minkowski p=2 == Euclidean,
which is the metric the paper names in Eq. (2) (assumption A1).

Requirements: R3 (bank built from normal-training tokens only), R4 (score = min
distance to the bank, larger = more anomalous).
"""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

REPO = os.path.abspath("repo")
if REPO not in sys.path:
    sys.path.insert(0, REPO)

from TokenCore import TokenCore  # noqa: E402  (authors' code, unmodified)


def fit_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=1):
    """Fit the memory bank on normal-training token embeddings and score test tokens."""
    X_train = np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float32)
    X_test = np.asarray(X_test, dtype=np.float32)
    assert X_train.shape[1] == X_test.shape[1] == 768, "expected 768-d BERT embeddings"
    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    model.fit(X_train)
    scores = np.asarray(model.decision_function(X_test), dtype=np.float64)
    assert scores.shape == (X_test.shape[0],), "one score per test token expected"
    assert np.all(np.isfinite(scores)), "non-finite token scores"
    return scores


def self_distance_control(X_train):
    """Sanity control (R4): distance of a training token to its own bank should be ~0
    when the token is excluded from its own nearest-neighbour search."""
    model = TokenCore(n_neighbors=2).fit(np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float32))
    d, _ = model.nbrs.kneighbors(np.asarray(X_train, dtype=np.float32))
    return d[:, 1]  # skip the self-match at distance 0

"""Metric layer: token-level and document-level AUROC / AUPRC.

Token level (paper Sec. 6.1 / R7): all test tokens of all test documents are pooled
into a single ranking -- this is exactly what the released Demo.ipynb does
(`roc_auc_score(z_test, score)` on the flattened matrices), see assumption A15.

Document level (paper Sec. 5 Eq. (3) / R5): s_doc = mean of the document's token scores.

AUPRC is computed the way the notebook imports it (precision_recall_curve + auc) and
also with sklearn's average_precision_score; both are reported.
"""
import numpy as np
from sklearn.metrics import average_precision_score, precision_recall_curve, roc_auc_score


def auroc(y, s):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    if len(np.unique(y)) < 2:
        return float("nan")
    return float(roc_auc_score(y, s))


def auprc(y, s):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    if len(np.unique(y)) < 2:
        return float("nan")
    prec, rec, _ = precision_recall_curve(y, s)
    return float(auc(rec, prec))


def ap(y, s):
    y = np.asarray(y).astype(int)
    if len(np.unique(y)) < 2:
        return float("nan")
    return float(average_precision_score(y, s))


def auc(x, y):
    """Trapezoidal area, mirroring sklearn.metrics.auc used in Demo.ipynb."""
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
    order = np.argsort(x)
    return float(np.trapezoid(y[order], x[order]))


def doc_scores(token_scores, doc_of, n_docs):
    """Mean aggregation of token scores within each document (Eq. (3), R5)."""
    sums = np.zeros(n_docs, dtype=np.float64)
    cnts = np.zeros(n_docs, dtype=np.float64)
    np.add.at(sums, doc_of, token_scores)
    np.add.at(cnts, doc_of, 1.0)
    assert np.all(cnts > 0), "a test document received no token scores"
    return sums / cnts


def evaluate(token_scores, token_labels, doc_of, n_test_docs, doc_labels):
    """Return the full metric dict for one (split, backbone) run."""
    token_scores = np.asarray(token_scores, dtype=np.float64)
    token_labels = np.asarray(token_labels).astype(int)
    doc_of = np.asarray(doc_of, dtype=int)
    doc_labels = np.asarray(doc_labels).astype(int)

    ds = doc_scores(token_scores, doc_of, n_test_docs)
    return {
        "token_auroc": auroc(token_labels, token_scores),
        "token_auprc": auprc(token_labels, token_scores),
        "token_ap": ap(token_labels, token_scores),
        "doc_auroc": auroc(doc_labels, ds),
        "doc_auprc": auprc(doc_labels, ds),
        "doc_ap": ap(doc_labels, ds),
        "n_test_tokens": int(len(token_labels)),
        "n_positive_tokens": int(token_labels.sum()),
        "token_positive_rate": float(token_labels.mean()),
        "n_test_docs": int(n_test_docs),
        "n_positive_docs": int(doc_labels.sum()),
    }


def random_control(token_labels, doc_labels, seed=0, n_rep=20):
    """Control run: random token scores should give AUROC ~0.5 and AUPRC ~ positive rate."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(seed)
    token_labels = np.asarray(token_labels).astype(int)
    doc_labels = np.asarray(doc_labels).astype(int)
    t, d = [], []
    for _ in range(n_rep):
        s = rng.rand(len(token_labels))
        t.append(auroc(token_labels, s))
        d.append(auroc(doc_labels, rng.rand(len(doc_labels))))
    return {"token_auroc_mean": float(np.mean(t)), "doc_auroc_mean": float(np.mean(d)),
            "n_rep": n_rep}


def metric_parity_check():
    """Verify the AUROC/AUPRC plumbing against sklearn on synthetic labels."""
    rng = np.random.RandomState(7)
    y = rng.randint(0, 2, 500)
    s = rng.rand(500) + 0.3 * y
    from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score as sk_auc
    ok_auc = abs(auroc(y, s) - sk_auc(y, s)) < 1e-9
    ok_ap = abs(ap(y, s) - average_precision_score(y, s)) < 1e-12
    return {"auroc_matches_sklearn": bool(ok_auc), "ap_matches_sklearn": bool(ok_ap)}

"""reproduce.py -- TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar benchmark (claim C1).

End-to-end, from scratch:
    repo/data/grammar.npy  (released benchmark, R10)
      -> 50%-of-normal train/test split (R6, A14)
      -> BERT-base word embeddings, element-wise max pooling over subwords
         (authors' repo/align.py, Eq. (1), R1/R2/R9)
      -> memory bank of normal-training token embeddings (R3)
      -> nearest-neighbour token scores (authors' repo/TokenCore.py, Eq. (2), R4)
      -> pooled token-level AUROC / AUPRC (R7, A15)
      -> mean-aggregated document-level AUROC / AUPRC (Eq. (3), R5)
      -> results/metrics.json

Primary configuration (manager decision A12): bert-base-cased, the backbone the
authors' released Demo.ipynb actually uses.  bert-base-uncased (the paper's stated
backbone) is run as a labelled sensitivity variant.

Usage:
    python reproduce.py                     # primary + sensitivity + multi-seed spread
    python reproduce.py --smoke             # 10-document end-to-end smoke test
    python reproduce.py --models uncased --seeds 0

    train_mask = np.isin(doc_of, train_idx)

    X_train, z_train = X[train_mask], z[train_mask]

    t0 = time.time()
    scores = detector.fit_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    fit_seconds = time.time() - t0

    doc_labels = [docs[i]["doc_label"] for i in test_idx]
    m = evaluate.evaluate(scores, z_test, doc_of_test, len(test_idx), doc_labels)

    m["n_bank_tokens"] = int(X_train.shape[0])

"""Sensitivity analysis over the ambiguities the paper does not pin down.

Run separately from reproduce.py (it is a search, not the default run):
    python src/sensitivity.py

Varied factors (all recorded in the assumption ledger):
  A14  split seed / split mechanism (shuffled seeds 0..9, and unshuffled file order)
  A1/A9  distance metric and embedding normalisation
       (Euclidean on raw embeddings  == the primary choice;
        L2-normalised + Euclidean   == cosine nearest neighbour)
  A13  n_neighbors (1 = paper's "nearest neighbor"; 5 = mean of 5 NN distances)

Writes sensitivity_log.json next to this file (outside results/).
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
os.chdir(ROOT)

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import detector  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402

MODELS = ["bert-base-cased", "bert-base-uncased"]
SEEDS = list(range(10))


def l2norm(X):
    n = np.linalg.norm(X, axis=1, keepdims=True)
    n[n == 0] = 1.0
    return X / n


def run(docs, emb, train_idx, test_idx, normalize=False, n_neighbors=1):
    X, z, doc_of = embed_bert.flatten(emb)
    if normalize:
        X = l2norm(X.astype(np.float64)).astype(np.float32)
    tr, te = np.isin(doc_of, train_idx), np.isin(doc_of, test_idx)
    X_train, X_test = X[tr], X[te]
    z_test, doc_of_test = z[te], doc_of[te]
    uniq, doc_of_test = np.unique(doc_of_test, return_inverse=True)
    scores = detector.fit_score(X_train, X_test, n_neighbors=n_neighbors)
    doc_labels = [docs[i]["doc_label"] for i in test_idx]
    return evaluate.evaluate(scores, z_test, doc_of_test, len(test_idx), doc_labels)


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    stats = data_grammar.check_dataset(docs)
    print("dataset:", stats)

    embs = {m: embed_bert.embed_all(docs, m) for m in MODELS}

    # split variants: shuffled seeds 0..9 + unshuffled file order
    splits = {f"shuffled_seed{s}": data_grammar.split_doc_indices(docs, seed=s) for s in SEEDS}
    normal_order = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d["doc_label"] == 0])
    anom = np.array([i for i, d in enumerate(docs) if d["doc_label"] == 1])
    half = len(normal_order) // 2
    splits["file_order"] = (normal_order[:half], np.concatenate([normal_order[half:], anom]))

    log = {"dataset_stats": stats, "variants": {}}

    def record(name, model, split_name, normalize, n_neighbors, m):
        log["variants"][name] = {
            "model": model, "split": split_name, "l2_normalized": normalize,
            "n_neighbors": n_neighbors,
            "token_auroc": round(m["token_auroc"], 4),
            "token_auprc": round(m["token_auprc"], 4),
            "doc_auroc": round(m["doc_auroc"], 4),
            "doc_auprc": round(m["doc_auprc"], 4),
        }

    for model in MODELS:
        for split_name, (tr, te) in splits.items():
            for normalize in (False, True):
                for k in (1, 5):
                    m = run(docs, embs[model], tr, te, normalize=normalize, n_neighbors=k)
                    record(f"{model}|{split_name}|norm={normalize}|k={k}",
                           model, split_name, normalize, k, m)

    # ---- summaries -------------------------------------------------------------
    def agg(model, normalize, k, split_names):
        vals = [log["variants"][f"{model}|{s}|norm={normalize}|k={k}"]["token_auroc"]
                for s in split_names]
        prc = [log["variants"][f"{model}|{s}|norm={normalize}|k={k}"]["token_auprc"]
               for s in split_names]
        return {"n_splits": len(vals), "token_auroc_mean": round(float(np.mean(vals)), 4),
                "token_auroc_std": round(float(np.std(vals)), 4),
                "token_auroc_min": round(float(np.min(vals)), 4),
                "token_auroc_max": round(float(np.max(vals)), 4),
                "token_auprc_mean": round(float(np.mean(prc)), 4),
                "token_auprc_std": round(float(np.std(prc)), 4)}

    shuffled = [f"shuffled_seed{s}" for s in SEEDS]
    log["summary"] = {}
    for model in MODELS:
        for normalize in (False, True):
            for k in (1, 5):
                key = f"{model}|norm={normalize}|k={k}"
                log["summary"][key] = {
                    "over_10_shuffled_splits": agg(model, normalize, k, shuffled),
                    "file_order_split": log["variants"][f"{model}|file_order|norm={normalize}|k={k}"],
                }

    out = os.path.join(HERE, "sensitivity_log.json")
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump(log, f, indent=2)

    print(f"\nwrote {out}  ({len(log['variants'])} variants)")
    print(f"{'variant':<44} {'auroc_mean':>10} {'std':>7} {'min':>7} {'max':>7} {'auprc_mean':>10}")
    for key, s in log["summary"].items():
        a = s["over_10_shuffled_splits"]
        print(f"{key:<44} {a['token_auroc_mean']:>10.4f} {a['token_auroc_std']:>7.4f} "
              f"{a['token_auroc_min']:>7.4f} {a['token_auroc_max']:>7.4f} {a['token_auprc_mean']:>10.4f}")
    print("\nfile-order (unshuffled) split:")
    for key, s in log["summary"].items():
        f_ = s["file_order_split"]
        print(f"  {key:<42} auroc={f_['token_auroc']:.4f} auprc={f_['token_auprc']:.4f}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Figure 1 illustrates the overall architecture. TokenCore adapts
the memory bank paradigm from PatchCore [10] in computer vision
to the text domain.
Embedding Extraction with Max Pooling. Given an input
text, we first obtain contextualized representations using pre-trained
language models such as BERT [4]. Since tokenizers often split
words into multiple subword units, we need to aggregate subword
embeddings to obtain word-level representations for alignment
with token-level annotations.
While existing approaches always use only the first subword’s
embedding or average pooling across subwords, these methods
may lose critical anomaly signals distributed across different sub-
word positions. To maximize the anomaly signal for each token,
we propose using max pooling to aggregate subword embeddings.
Specifically, for a word split into nsubwords with embeddings
{e1, e2, . . . , en}, the token-level embedding is computed as:
etoken = max(e1, e2, . . . , en)
(1)
where the max operation is applied element-wise across each em-
bedding dimension. This aggregation strategy ensures that the
strongest signal from any subword position is preserved, which
is particularly important for anomaly detection where abnormal
patterns may manifest in specific subword positions.

number of tokens in the normal training data.

bedding etest, we compute its anomaly score as the distance to its
nearest neighbor in the memory bank:
stoken = min
m∈M d(etest, m)

where d(·, ·) denotes the distance metric (e.g., Euclidean distance).
A larger distance indicates higher anomaly score, as the token is

"""Independent verification of the document-level path (no TokenCore class, no align.py).

Recomputes, from scratch with plain numpy:
  * word embeddings by element-wise max pooling over subwords (Eq. 1)
  * memory bank from normal-training tokens only (R3)
  * token score = min L2 distance to the bank (Eq. 2)
  * document score = mean of the document's token scores (Eq. 3)
and compares against reproduce.py's numbers.  Also prints the per-document score
distributions so a label-alignment bug would be obvious.
"""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
os.chdir(ROOT)

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score  # noqa: E402


def brute_force(docs, emb, train_idx, test_idx):
    X, z, doc_of = embed_bert.flatten(emb)
    tr = np.isin(doc_of, train_idx)
    te = np.isin(doc_of, test_idx)
    bank = X[tr].astype(np.float64)
    Xte = X[te].astype(np.float64)
    zte = z[te]
    dte = doc_of[te]

    # min L2 distance to the bank, computed with an explicit double loop over dims
    d2 = ((Xte[:, None, :] - bank[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(-1)
    scores = np.sqrt(d2.min(axis=1))

    uniq = np.unique(dte)
    doc_scores, doc_labels = [], []
    for u in uniq:
        m = dte == u
        doc_scores.append(scores[m].mean())
        doc_labels.append(docs[int(u)]["doc_label"])
    return scores, zte, np.array(doc_scores), np.array(doc_labels), uniq


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    emb = embed_bert.embed_all(docs, "bert-base-uncased")
    for seed in (0, 1, 2):
        train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_doc_indices(docs, seed=seed)
        s, z, ds, dl, uniq = brute_force(docs, emb, train_idx, test_idx)
        print(f"\n=== seed {seed} ===")
        print(f"  test tokens={len(s)} pos={int(z.sum())}  test docs={len(ds)} pos_docs={int(dl.sum())}")
        print(f"  token AUROC  = {roc_auc_score(z, s):.4f}")
        print(f"  doc   AUROC  = {roc_auc_score(dl, ds):.4f}")
        print(f"  mean token score: normal docs={ds[dl == 0].mean():.3f}  anomalous docs={ds[dl == 1].mean():.3f}")
        print(f"  median token score: normal={np.median(s[z == 0]):.3f} anomalous={np.median(s[z == 1]):.3f}")
        # max-aggregation control (NOT the paper's Eq. 3, diagnostic only)
        dmax = []
        for u in uniq:
            m = dte_of(dte, u)
            dmax.append(s[m].max())
        print(f"  doc AUROC (max agg, diagnostic only) = {roc_auc_score(dl, np.array(dmax)):.4f}")
        # show the 5 highest-scoring documents
        order = np.argsort(-ds)[:5]
        for o in order:
            print(f"    doc {uniq[o]:>3} label={dl[o]} mean_score={ds[o]:.3f} "
                  f"n_tok={(dte == uniq[o]).sum()} n_pos={int(z[dte == uniq[o]].sum())}")


def dte_of(dte, u):
    return dte == u


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Independent verification of the document-level path (seed 0 only, cached embeddings).

Recomputes, from scratch with plain numpy (no TokenCore class, no align.py, no sklearn
neighbours):
  * word embeddings by element-wise max pooling over subwords (Eq. 1)
  * memory bank from normal-training tokens only (R3)
  * token score = min L2 distance to the bank (Eq. 2)
  * document score = mean of the document's token scores (Eq. 3)
and compares against reproduce.py's numbers, so a label-alignment bug would show up
as a disagreement.  Distances are computed in chunks to stay inside memory.
"""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
os.chdir(ROOT)

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score  # noqa: E402


def min_l2(X, bank, chunk=256):
    out = np.empty(len(X), dtype=np.float64)
    for i in range(0, len(X), chunk):
        blk = X[i:i + chunk].astype(np.float64)
        d2 = ((blk[:, None, :] - bank[None, :, :]) ** 2).sum(-1)
        out[i:i + chunk] = np.sqrt(d2.min(axis=1))
    return out


def main(seed=0, model="bert-base-uncased"):
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    emb = embed_bert.embed_all(docs, model)          # served from the on-disk cache
    train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_doc_indices(docs, seed=seed)

    X, z, doc_of = embed_bert.flatten(emb)
    tr, te = np.isin(doc_of, train_idx), np.isin(doc_of, test_idx)
    bank, Xte, zte, dte = X[tr], X[te], z[te], doc_of[te]

    scores = min_l2(Xte, bank)
    uniq = np.unique(dte)
    doc_scores = np.array([scores[dte == u].mean() for u in uniq])
    doc_labels = np.array([docs[int(u)]["doc_label"] for u in uniq])

    print(f"model={model} seed={seed}")
    print(f"  bank tokens={len(bank)}  test tokens={len(scores)} (pos={int(zte.sum())})  "
          f"test docs={len(uniq)} (pos={int(doc_labels.sum())})")
    print(f"  token AUROC = {roc_auc_score(zte, scores):.4f}")
    print(f"  doc   AUROC = {roc_auc_score(doc_labels, doc_scores):.4f}   (Eq. 3 mean aggregation)")
    print(f"  mean token score: normal docs={doc_scores[doc_labels == 0].mean():.3f}  "
          f"anomalous docs={doc_scores[doc_labels == 1].mean():.3f}")
    print(f"  median token score: normal={np.median(scores[zte == 0]):.3f}  "
          f"anomalous={np.median(scores[zte == 1]):.3f}")
    dmax = np.array([scores[dte == u].max() for u in uniq])
    print(f"  doc AUROC (max aggregation, diagnostic only) = {roc_auc_score(doc_labels, dmax):.4f}")
    print("  top-5 scoring documents:")
    for o in np.argsort(-doc_scores)[:5]:
        m = dte == uniq[o]
        print(f"    doc {uniq[o]:>3} label={doc_labels[o]} mean={doc_scores[o]:.3f} "
              f"n_tok={int(m.sum())} n_pos={int(zte[m].sum())}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def check_special_and_punct(docs, emb, model_name):
    """A4 verification: [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] must never enter the memory bank or be scored,
    and punctuation-only word units must be handled the way the released labels mark them.

    align.py skips every subword whose word_ids() entry is None, which is exactly the set
    {[CLS], [SEP], [PAD]}; the 1:1 assertion in embed_all then guarantees that the number
    of scored word units equals the number of gold word tokens.  Here we confirm both
    statements directly on the tokenizer and report the punctuation statistics.
    """
    from transformers import AutoTokenizer
    tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)

    # 1. special tokens: word_ids() is None exactly at the special-token positions
    sample = docs[0]["words"]
    enc = tok(sample, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt")
    wids = enc.word_ids(0)
    none_pos = [i for i, w in enumerate(wids) if w is None]
    ids = enc["input_ids"][0].tolist()
    special_at_none = [tok.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids[i]) for i in none_pos]
    n_word_units = len([w for w in wids if w is not None])

    # 2. punctuation-only gold tokens: are they stored / scored, and are any anomalous?
    import string
    punct_idx = [i for i, w in enumerate(docs[0]["words"]) if w in string.punctuation]
    all_punct = [(i, d["words"][i], d["token_labels"][i])
                 for d in docs for i in range(len(d["words"]))
                 if d["words"][i] in string.punctuation]
    n_punct = len(all_punct)
    n_punct_anom = sum(1 for _, _, l in all_punct if l == 1)

    return {
        "special_token_positions_are_none_word_id": none_pos,
        "tokens_at_those_positions": special_at_none,
        "n_word_units_sample_doc": n_word_units,
        "n_gold_tokens_sample_doc": len(sample),
        "word_units_equal_gold_tokens": n_word_units == len(sample),
        "n_punctuation_only_tokens_all_docs": n_punct,
        "n_punctuation_only_tokens_labeled_anomalous": n_punct_anom,
        "punctuation_units_are_scored_and_stored": True,
        "note": ("punctuation is a gold word token in the released annotation, so it is "
                 "embedded, stored in the bank and scored like any other word unit (R9); "
                 "only [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] are excluded, by align.py's word_ids() is None skip"),
    }

"""The authors' released path, run verbatim on the released data/grammar.npy.

Mirrors repo/demo.ipynb cell 1 exactly:
    data = np.load(r'data\\grammar.npy', allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens, labels, sentence_labels = data['tokens'], data['labels'], ...
    X_train, y_train, X_test, y_test, z_train, z_test = eval.split_anomaly_data(...)
    embeddings = extract_word_embeddings(model, tokenizer, X_train)   # align.py
    model = TextCore(); model.fit(embeddings); score = model.decision_function(...)
    roc_auc_score(z_test, score)

The two modules the notebook imports but the repo does not ship are reconstructed here:
  * eval.split_anomaly_data  -> src/data_grammar.split_doc_indices (50% of normal docs, R6)
  * TextCore                 -> repo/TokenCore.py's TokenCore (same memory-bank + 1-NN API)

Running this on the SAME split as reproduce.py separates data/split errors from
embedding/scoring errors: if this number equals reproduce.py's, the divergence from the
paper is in the representation/scoring step, not in the data handling.
"""
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "repo"))
os.chdir(ROOT)

from sklearn.metrics import roc_auc_score  # noqa: E402

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
from align import extract_word_embeddings  # noqa: E402  (authors' code, unmodified)
from TokenCore import TokenCore  # noqa: E402  (authors' code, unmodified)

MODEL_NAME = "bert-base-uncased"  # paper Sec. 6.1 / R1


def main(seed=0):
    # ---- exactly the notebook's data loading -------------------------------------
    data = np.load(r"repo/data/grammar.npy", allow_pickle=True).item()
    tokens = data["tokens"]
    labels = data["labels"]
    sentence_labels = [1 if any(labels) else 0 for labels in labels]
    print("type:", type(data), "keys:", list(data.keys()))
    print("n docs:", len(tokens), "n anomalous docs:", sum(sentence_labels))

    # ---- reconstructed eval.split_anomaly_data (R6: 50% of normal docs) ----------
    train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_doc_indices(
        [{"words": t, "token_labels": l, "doc_label": s}
         for t, l, s in zip(tokens, labels, sentence_labels)], seed=seed)
    X_train = [tokens[i] for i in train_idx]
    X_test = [tokens[i] for i in test_idx]
    z_train = [labels[i] for i in train_idx]
    z_test = [labels[i] for i in test_idx]
    print(f"split seed={seed}: {len(X_train)} train docs, {len(X_test)} test docs, "
          f"{sum(sum(z) for z in z_train)} anomalous train tokens")

    # ---- authors' align.py, verbatim --------------------------------------------
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
    model.eval()

    train_emb = extract_word_embeddings(model, tokenizer, X_train)
    test_emb = extract_word_embeddings(model, tokenizer, X_test)
    print("train embeddings:", train_emb.shape, " test embeddings:", test_emb.shape)

    # ---- authors' TokenCore.py, verbatim ----------------------------------------
    detector = TokenCore()
    detector.fit(train_emb)
    score = detector.decision_function(test_emb)
    print("score shape:", np.asarray(score).shape)

    y_true = np.concatenate([np.asarray(z, dtype=int) for z in z_test])
    y_score = np.asarray(score).reshape(-1)
    assert len(y_true) == len(y_score), (len(y_true), len(y_score))
    print(f"\nRELEASED PATH (verbatim align.py + TokenCore.py, {MODEL_NAME}, seed {seed})")
    print(f"  token-level AUROC = {roc_auc_score(y_true, y_score):.4f}")
    print(f"  n test tokens = {len(y_true)}, n anomalous = {int(y_true.sum())}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

def _hidden(hidden_states, layer_mode):
    """A3: which BERT layer(s) feed the max pooling.  'last' = outputs.last_hidden_state
    (align.py's choice, and the primary configuration); 'mean_last4' = mean of the last
    four hidden states (the other common convention)."""
    if layer_mode == "last":

def embed_documents_variant(all_tokens, all_labels, model_name, device="cpu",
                            layer_mode="last", normalize=False):
    """Ablation front-end: identical pooling to align.py (element-wise max over the
    subwords of each word, skipping word_id None = [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD]) but with the
    hidden-state source (A3) and an optional L2 normalisation (A9) as switches.

    align.py itself hardcodes outputs.last_hidden_state, so it cannot express these
    variants; this function is a faithful re-implementation of its pooling loop and is
    only used for the ablations, never for the primary configuration.
    """
    import torch
    from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer

    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device).eval()

    result = []
    with torch.no_grad():
        for tokens, labels in zip(all_tokens, all_labels):
            encoded = tokenizer(tokens, is_split_into_words=True, return_tensors="pt",
                                truncation=True, padding=False)
            out = model(input_ids=encoded["input_ids"].to(device),
                        attention_mask=encoded["attention_mask"].to(device),
                        output_hidden_states=True)
            hidden = _hidden(out.hidden_states, layer_mode)[0]  # (seq, 768)
            word_ids = encoded.word_ids(batch_index=0)

            sent, prev, cur = [], None, []
            for pos, wid in enumerate(word_ids):
                if wid is None:
                    continue
                vec = hidden[pos].cpu().numpy()
                if wid != prev:
                    if cur:
                        sent.append({"token": cur[0], "embedding": np.max(np.stack(cur[1]), axis=0),
                                     "label": cur[2]})
                    cur = [tokens[wid], [vec], labels[wid] if labels is not None else None]
                else:
                    cur[1].append(vec)
                prev = wid
            if cur:
                sent.append({"token": cur[0], "embedding": np.max(np.stack(cur[1]), axis=0),
                             "label": cur[2]})
            result.append(sent)

    if normalize:
        for sent in result:
            for item in sent:
                v = np.asarray(item["embedding"], dtype=np.float32)
                n = float(np.linalg.norm(v))
                item["embedding"] = v / n if n > 0 else v
    return result

"""A3 / A9 ablations on the Grammar token-level claim (seed 0 only).

The manager's hypothesis: the identical mean token score for normal vs. anomalous
documents suggests the L2 nearest-neighbour distance is tracking the embedding NORM
rather than direction.  Two separate ablations test that:

  A3  hidden-state source : last hidden layer (align.py / primary) vs. mean of the last four
  A9  normalisation      : raw embeddings (primary) vs. L2-normalised (== cosine NN)

Each variant is scored with the authors' TokenCore.py on the same seed-0 split.
Writes src/ablations_log.json (outside results/).
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
os.chdir(ROOT)

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import detector  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402

MODEL = "bert-base-uncased"  # paper Sec. 6.1 / R1
SEED = 0

VARIANTS = [
    ("paper_config (A3=last hidden, A9=raw)", dict(layer_mode="last", normalize=False)),
    ("A3=mean of last 4 hidden layers", dict(layer_mode="mean_last4", normalize=False)),
    ("A9=L2-normalised embeddings", dict(layer_mode="last", normalize=True)),
    ("A3=mean last 4 + A9=L2-normalised", dict(layer_mode="mean_last4", normalize=True)),
]


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_doc_indices(docs, seed=SEED)
    tr = set(int(i) for i in train_idx)
    te = set(int(i) for i in test_idx)

    results = {}
    for name, kw in VARIANTS:
        emb = embed_bert.embed_all(docs, MODEL, **kw)
        X, z, doc_of = embed_bert.flatten(emb)
        X_train, z_train = X[[i for i in range(len(X)) if doc_of[i] in tr]], None
        mask_tr = np.isin(doc_of, list(tr))
        mask_te = np.isin(doc_of, list(te))
        X_train, X_test = X[mask_tr], X[mask_te]
        z_test = z[mask_te]
        doc_of_test = doc_of[mask_te]

        scores = detector.fit_score(X_train, X_test)
        uniq, doc_of_test = np.unique(doc_of_test, return_inverse=True)
        doc_labels = [docs[int(i)]["doc_label"] for i in uniq]
        m = evaluate.evaluate(scores, z_test, doc_of_test, len(uniq), doc_labels)

        # norm diagnostic: is the distance tracking the embedding norm?
        norms = np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1)
        results[name] = {
            "token_auroc": round(m["token_auroc"], 4),
            "token_auprc": round(m["token_auprc"], 4),
            "doc_auroc": round(m["doc_auroc"], 4),
            "mean_test_token_norm": round(float(norms.mean()), 3),
            "corr(score, norm)": round(float(np.corrcoef(scores, norms)[0, 1]), 4),
            "mean_score_normal_tokens": round(float(scores[z_test == 0].mean()), 3),
            "mean_score_anomalous_tokens": round(float(scores[z_test == 1].mean()), 3),
        }
        print(f"{name:42s} token_auroc={results[name]['token_auroc']:.4f} "
              f"token_auprc={results[name]['token_auprc']:.4f} "
              f"doc_auroc={results[name]['doc_auroc']:.4f} "
              f"corr(score,norm)={results[name]['corr(score, norm)']:.3f}")

    out = os.path.join(HERE, "ablations_log.json")
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
        json.dump({"model": MODEL, "seed": SEED, "target_token_auroc": 0.6371,
                   "variants": results}, f, indent=2)
    print("wrote", out)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

"""Diagnostic grid on the Grammar token-level claim (seed 0 only).

2 x 2 x 2 = 8 cells:
  A3  hidden-state source : last hidden layer  |  mean of the last 4 hidden layers
  A9  normalisation       : raw hidden states  |  L2-normalised
  A1  distance metric     : Euclidean          |  cosine

This is a SENSITIVITY DIAGNOSTIC, not a search for the target: the primary configuration
is fixed by the paper (Sec. 6.1 / R1: BERT-base-uncased, max pooling) and by the released
code (align.py + TokenCore.py), and reproduce.py is unchanged.

What the released code hardcodes (read off repo/align.py and repo/TokenCore.py):
  * align.py line 84   : outputs.last_hidden_state            -> A3 = last hidden layer
  * align.py line 123  : np.max(np.stack(current_subwords))   -> element-wise max pooling
  * align.py line 117  : `if word_idx is None: continue`       -> [CLS]/[SEP]/[PAD] excluded
  * align.py line 42   : model_name default 'bert-base-cased'  (notebook passes it explicitly)
  * TokenCore.py line 8 : n_neighbors=1                        -> nearest neighbour, k=1
  * TokenCore.py line 36: NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1)      -> default metric = Minkowski
                                                                    p=2 == Euclidean (A1)
  * no normalisation anywhere                                  -> A9 = raw hidden states
So the released path is exactly cell (last, raw, Euclidean).

Writes src/ablations_log.json (outside results/).
"""
import json
import os
import sys

import numpy as np

HERE = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
ROOT = os.path.dirname(HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, HERE)
sys.path.insert(0, os.path.join(ROOT, "repo"))
os.chdir(ROOT)

import data_grammar  # noqa: E402
import embed_bert  # noqa: E402
import evaluate  # noqa: E402
from sklearn.neighbors import NearestNeighbors  # noqa: E402

MODEL = "bert-base-uncased"  # paper Sec. 6.1 / R1
SEED = 0
TARGET = 0.6371


def score(X_train, X_test, metric):
    """Same scoring as the authors' TokenCore.decision_function, with the metric as a
    switch (TokenCore.py hardcodes NearestNeighbors' default = Euclidean)."""
    nn = NearestNeighbors(n_neighbors=1, metric=metric).fit(X_train)
    d, _ = nn.kneighbors(X_test)
    return d[:, 0]


def main():
    docs = data_grammar.load_grammar()
    train_idx, test_idx = data_grammar.split_doc_indices(docs, seed=SEED)
    tr = set(int(i) for i in train_idx)
    te = set(int(i) for i in test_idx)

    rows = []
    for layer_mode in ["last", "mean_last4"]:
        emb = embed_bert.embed_all(docs, MODEL, layer_mode=layer_mode, normalize=False)
        X, z, doc_of = embed_bert.flatten(emb)
        m_tr, m_te = np.isin(doc_of, list(tr)), np.isin(doc_of, list(te))
        X_train, X_test = X[m_tr], X[m_te]
        z_test, doc_of_test = z[m_te], doc_of[m_te]
        uniq, doc_of_test = np.unique(doc_of_test, return_inverse=True)
        doc_labels = [docs[int(i)]["doc_label"] for i in uniq]

        for normalize in [False, True]:
            Xtr = X_train / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X_train, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12) \
                if normalize else X_train
            Xte = X_test / np.maximum(np.linalg.norm(X_test, axis=1, keepdims=True), 1e-12) \
                if normalize else X_test
            for metric in ["euclidean", "cosine"]:
                s = score(Xtr, Xte, metric)
                m = evaluate.evaluate(s, z_test, doc_of_test, len(uniq), doc_labels)
                rows.append({
                    "A3_hidden": layer_mode,
                    "A9_norm": "L2-normalised" if normalize else "raw",
                    "A1_metric": metric,
                    "token_auroc": round(m["token_auroc"], 4),
                    "token_auprc": round(m["token_auprc"], 4),
                    "doc_auroc": round(m["doc_auroc"], 4),
                    "is_released_config": (layer_mode == "last" and not normalize
                                           and metric == "euclidean"),
                })

    print(f"\n{'A3 hidden':12s} {'A9 norm':14s} {'A1 metric':10s} "
          f"{'token AUROC':>12s} {'token AUPRC':>12s} {'doc AUROC':>10s}  released?")
    print("-" * 82)
    for r in rows:
        print(f"{r['A3_hidden']:12s} {r['A9_norm']:14s} {r['A1_metric']:10s} "
              f"{r['token_auroc']:12.4f} {r['token_auprc']:12.4f} {r['doc_auroc']:10.4f}"
              f"  {'<== released code' if r['is_released_config'] else ''}")

    vals = [r["token_auroc"] for r in rows]
    print(f"\nspread over the 8 cells: min={min(vals):.4f} max={max(vals):.4f} "
          f"mean={np.mean(vals):.4f} std={np.std(vals):.4f}")
    print(f"target (paper Table 1, Grammar ROC) = {TARGET}")

    # the two L2-normalised cells must agree: on unit vectors Euclidean and cosine
    # distance are monotonically related, so the AUROC is identical
    a = [r for r in rows if r["A9_norm"] == "L2-normalised" and r["A3_hidden"] == "last"]
    print(f"L2-normalised: euclidean={a[0]['token_auroc']:.4f} cosine={a[1]['token_auroc']:.4f} "
          f"(identical by construction: d_euclid^2 = 2(1-cos) on unit vectors)")

    out = os.path.join(HERE, "ablations_log.json")
    with open(out, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:

                   "note": "sensitivity diagnostic, not a search; reproduce.py unchanged",

metrics.split: token-level: 50% of the 270 normal documents form the memory-bank training set; the remaining 135 normal + all 30 anomalous documents are the test set; all test tokens pooled into one ranking

config.pooling: element-wise max over subword embeddings (Eq. 1, authors' align.py)
config.memory_bank: all word-level embeddings of all tokens of the 135 normal training docs
config.token_score: min Euclidean distance to the memory bank (Eq. 2, authors' TokenCore.py)

target.statement: TokenCore token-level AUROC on the Grammar dataset
target.table_ref: Table 1, Token section, row TokenCore, column Grammar ROC

tolerance.why: Rule 3: AUROC is a bounded score and the paper prints it in [0,1] as a fraction; no std/CI over repeated runs is reported (rule 1 inapplicable), and the token-level test set for Grammar is only ~150 documents' tokens, whose size is never stated as 2,000+ examples, so the smaller-set band of 0.02 absolute is used rather than the 0.01 of rule 2.

audit_summary: The C1 reproduction is methodologically faithful: it loads the released 300-document Grammar benchmark with 270 normal + 30 anomalous documents, uses the authors' align.py and TokenCore.py, builds a normal-only token memory bank, scores tokens by 1-NN Euclidean distance, and aggregates by mean for document scores. The primary bert-base-uncased seed-0 run gives token-level AUROC 0.5978 versus the paper's 0.6371, with absolute error 0.0393, outside the 0.02 tolerance. The bert-base-cased sensitivity run is closer (0.6583 at seed 0, 0.6485 with file-order split), and the per-document-averaged AUROC for the primary run is 0.6509, which is within tolerance; thus the A5 token-level aggregation ambiguity is a plausible major source of the mismatch. No result appears hard-coded: the paper target 0.6371 is present only as a comparison constant, and all reported values are computed from embeddings and labels. The main requirement gap is R8: the six baseline methods were never implemented, so the comparison table is not reproduced, while the core TokenCore requirements R2-R7 and R9-R11 are met.

requirement_check.evidence: The primary TokenCore path uses BERT-base-uncased embeddings with the authors' max-pooling align.py, but none of the baseline methods were implemented, so the requirement that all methods (including baselines) share this representation cannot be satisfied.
embed_bert.embed_all defaults to repo/align.extract_word_embeddings, which performs element-wise max pooling over subwords; the alignment assertion confirms word units equal gold tokens.
run_one builds the memory bank only from train_mask documents and asserts z_train.sum()==0; the 135 normal training docs produce 1,202 normal token embeddings.
detector.fit_score wraps the released TokenCore(n_neighbors=1), using sklearn NearestNeighbors Euclidean distance (Minkowski p=2); self-match control distance is ~3.1e-7.
evaluate.doc_scores computes the mean of token scores per document; document-level AUROC/AUPRC are reported.
data_grammar.split_doc_indices shuffles normal documents and uses 50% for training; the test set is remaining normal plus all 30 anomalous documents (135 train docs, 165 test docs).
evaluate returns token_auroc, token_auprc, doc_auroc, and doc_auprc, and metrics.json records all four.
No LOF, iForest, ECOD, DeepSVDD, AutoEncoder, or LUNAR implementations or results appear; only TokenCore plus random/self-match controls are present.
Word-level aggregation is performed by align.py and embed_bert asserts one word unit per gold token; [CLS]/[SEP] are excluded via word_id None.
dataset_stats reports n_docs=300, n_normal_docs=270, n_anomalous_docs=30, doc_anomaly_rate=0.1.
data_grammar.load_grammar sets doc_label=1 iff any token label is 1, and check_dataset asserts this consistency for all documents.
